h: Making the Mitzvah an Inheritance That Endures

p: "And it shall be, when Hashem your God brings you
אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בָא שָׁמָּה
into the land which you are going to
In the Sifrei (on this parshah, Sifrei Devarim 55):
"Accept upon yourself the mitzvah stated here,
in reward for which you will come and inherit."
for it speaks of when they will come
and Yehoshua will apportion it to them.
But in the pasuk one must note
שֶׁתֵּיבוֹת אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בָא שָׁמָּה לְרִשְׁתָּהּ
that the words "which you are going to possess"
"when Hashem brings you into the land
that is, from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
that it will be like an inheritance that has no interruption
"Accept upon yourself the mitzvah stated here,
in reward for which you will come and inherit"
that it will be like an inheritance that has no interruption,
אַךְ יֵשׁ לְהָבִין מַה שֶּׁאָמַר הַלָּשׁוֹן
But one must understand the wording it used,
to which mitzvah does it refer?
רַק מִצְוַת וְנָתַתָּה אֶת הַבְּרָכָה וְגוֹמֵר
except the mitzvah of "you shall set the blessing," etc.;
and how is this mitzvah different,
that in its merit they would merit
an inheritance that has no interruption,
when there are mitzvos more stringent than it?
And if it refers to what is said
at the beginning of the parshah (Devarim 11:27),
אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶל מִצְוֹת ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם
"if you will listen to the mitzvos of Hashem your God"
there "mitzvos" is written in the plural,
and it refers to all the mitzvos,
whereas in the Sifrei it said
"accept upon yourself a mitzvah," in the singular.
עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּסוֹף פָּרָשָׁה הָעֲבָרָה
to what is said at the end of the previous parshah
דִּכְתִיב גַּם כֵּן מִצְוָה לְשׁוֹן יָחִיד
where "mitzvah" is also written in the singular.
in reward for which you will come and inherit."
But there too one must understand
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ (רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ד, ד)
In the Midrash (Rabbah on this parshah, Devarim Rabbah 4:4)
רַבִּי לֵוִי אָמַר זוֹ קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
Rabbi Levi said, "This is the reading of Shema,"
and the Rabbis said, "This is Shabbos."
that it is the reading of Shema,
to the parshah of "Vehayah im shamo'a,"
which ends just before it there.
אַךְ שָׁם גַּם כֵּן כְּתִיב (דְּבָרִים יא, יג)
But there too it is written (Devarim 11:13):
"And it shall be, if you will diligently listen
and it refers to all the mitzvos.
But it seems that the pasuk
does in truth refer to all the mitzvos,
and it said it in the singular,
כִּי אִם שָׁמוֹר תִּשְׁמְרוּן אֶת כָּל הַמִּצְוָה
"for if you diligently keep all the mitzvah"
is that the mitzvah should be
and that it be fixed in the heart,
And this is the meaning of the word "this":
that it be as explicit to the eye
as one who points with a finger,
That is, that it be fixed in the heart,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁדָּרְשׁוּ (מְגִילָּה טו, ב)
in the manner of what they expounded (Megillah 15b)
"Yet all this is worth nothing to me"
that all the treasures of that wicked one
And when something is engraved in the heart,
as though it stood before his eyes
and he pointed with a finger and said, "This."
And it said "which I command you";
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים לג, ד)
It is in the manner of what is said (Devarim 33:4):
and it is not written "Moshe wrote for us,"
for Hashem Yisbarach is the One who commands.
the light of Torah into the heart of all Yisrael,
"an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov";
for every single one of Yisrael
has a portion in the Torah,
who are called "the house of Yaakov"
And this is what they said in the Midrash
"'The congregation of Yannai' is not written here,
and it is with the intent stated.
And this is what it said:
which I command you to do it";
the intent in saying "to do it"
is in the manner of what they said in the Gemara
"as if he had made the words of Torah," etc.,
"as if he had made himself," etc.;
וְהַיְינוּ הַנֵּר ה׳ נִשְׁמַת אָדָם (מִשְׁלֵי כ, כז)
that is, "the lamp of Hashem is the soul of man" (Mishlei 20:27)
And this is what is said, "to do it":
as if he had made the mitzvah,
just as "as if he had made the words of Torah."
that it be fixed in the heart
both of them are to be done from your side.
to walk in all His ways, and to cleave to Him."
the holiness of the three Avos.
נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponds to the holiness of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
כְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponds to the holiness of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
from whose side come the words of Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג פ, ב)
comes from the side of Gevurah";
"Happy are those whose way is wholehearted,
who walk in the Torah of Hashem."
זֶהוּ קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
this is the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
whose holiness is cleaving to Hashem,
"But you who cleave to Hashem your God";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פ, ז)
from the passage about that wicked one:
he had a cleaving of the soul,
so too "you who cleave to Hashem"
is a cleaving of the soul;
וְזֶהוּ מִקְּדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and this is from the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him.
"Then will Hashem drive out," etc., "and you shall possess," etc.
that it be like an inheritance that has no interruption.
"Every place on which the sole of your foot
"the fear of you and the dread of you
that you shall tread upon," etc.
What is the relevance of "that you shall tread"?
Surely Yehoshua is the one who conquers
and apportions to Yisrael and divides it among them.
But this is from the holiness of Yaakov Avinu,
"And you shall spread out to the west and to the east," etc.;
that is, in every place where he treads
there will be the holiness of Eretz Yisrael.
And this is the inheritance of Yaakov,
which one merits through keeping Shabbos (Shabbos 118a).
And this is why it concludes (Devarim 11:25):
רְאֵה אָנֹכִי נוֹתֵן לִפְנֵיכֶם הַיּוֹם וְגוֹמֵר
"See, I set before you this day," etc.,
to the mitzvos of Hashem your God
which I command you this day."
According to its plain sense, that it refers to all the mitzvos,
the word "this day" does not fit.
אַךְ קָאֵי עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר לְעֵיל
But it refers to what is said above:
"which I command you to do it";
and as we said, the intent
is to "make" the words of Torah,
and that the mitzvah be explicit
And this is why it then says "Vehayah,"
which is a term of joy:
of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah
for so the name "Hashem your God" indicates,
is the Master of your powers;
אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בָא שָׁמָּה
"into the land which you are going to."
that is, Hashem Yisbarach from His side;
that you merit for it to be forever,
like an inheritance that has no interruption.
On this it said in the Sifrei,
it did not say "do the mitzvah,"
in the way that it said in the Sifrei
on the passage "When He enlarges" (Sifrei Devarim 75):
"Do the mitzvah stated in the passage,
in reward for which He will enlarge," etc.;
And that is what is said:
which is to "make" the words of Torah,
until it is as explicit to the eye,
"In reward for which you will come and inherit,"
וְהוֹרִישׁ ה׳ אֶת כָּל הַגּוֹיִם וְגוֹמֵר
"Then will Hashem drive out all these nations," etc.,
like an inheritance that has no interruption,
וְלִזְכּוֹת לִקְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and to merit the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,

p: which Hashem your God gives you to inherit,
and He gives you rest from all your enemies round about,
It is like what is said
"And you shall dwell in your land safely";
and it is written after it (Vayikra 26:6):
"And I will give peace in the land,
and you shall lie down and none shall make you afraid";
if there is no peace, there is nothing
the verse teaches: 'And I will give peace,'" etc.
And the main peace is from the evil inclination,
"There is no peace in my bones
And this is what is said:
"And I will give peace in the land,"
and then "you shall lie down and none shall make you afraid";
for a person has agitation and dread
from the war with the evil inclination,
and when one merits peace from the evil inclination,
"you shall lie down and none shall make you afraid."
which Hashem your God gives you to inherit,"
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יב, ב)
according to what is written (Rosh Hashanah 12b):
"Just as an inheritance has no interruption."
"And He gives you rest from all your enemies":
that is, from the evil inclination,
גַּם אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִים אִתּוֹ (מִשְׁלֵי טז, ז)
"He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him" (Mishlei 16:7)
that is, from all three kelipos,
the three roots of the kelipos.
in the manner of what is said:
"you shall lie down and none shall make you afraid."
That is, one merits the Supernal Shabbos,
where the evil inclination is cleared away from there
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּקּוּן מח, פה, א)
(as is written in Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48, 85a),
or agitation from the evil inclination;
"and you dwell," in settledness and rest, "in safety."
